## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A two-fascicle (上下) Sino-Japanese Vinaya disputation of *Jiādìng* 嘉定 2 (1209), assembled from the questions submitted by the Japanese pilgrim **Shunjō** 俊芿 ([俊芿](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BF%8A%E8%8A%BF), 1166–1227) — at that point in his twelve-year sojourn in Sòng China and shortly to return to Japan to found *Sennyū-ji* 泉涌寺 — together with the line-by-line answers separately supplied by **three Sòng Vinaya masters**: *Línānfǔ Bùkōng jiàoyuàn* 臨安府不空教院 [了然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BA%86%E7%84%B6) *Zhìyǒng Liǎorán* (1077–1141 — but see note below), *Huìjī jùn Yáojiāng Jílèzuòzhǔ* 會稽郡姚江極樂座主 [智瑞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E7%91%9E) *Zhìruì*, and *Zhīyán Jìnghuái Jìngfàn* 芝嵓淨懷淨梵 [妙音](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A6%99%E9%9F%B3) *Miàoyīn*. The catalog meta gives the principal author's name as *Jùnnǎi* 俊艿; the source signatures and DILA A000811 alike give 俊芿 (modern Japanese *Shunjō*).

**Abstract**

The *Lǜzōng wèndá* preserves **the most substantial early-thirteenth-century Sino-Japanese exchange on Vinaya doctrine**: thirty questions across two fascicles, treating the foundational doctrinal frame of the *Nánshān* Vinaya tradition. The questions are organized around discrete *疑* (*yí*, "doubts" / topics of inquiry); the surviving topic-headings include: *Sānguān shǐchū yí* 三觀始出疑 (the *Nánshān* threefold-contemplation programme: its origin and inheritance from the *Chán* master [道整](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E6%95%B4) Dàozhěng); *Sānguānjiāo míngyì yí* 三觀名義疑 (terminology of the three contemplations); *Sānguān shōujiào yí* 三觀收教疑 (which doctrinal-classification scheme the three contemplations subsume); *Nánshān lìzōng wéishī yí* 南山立宗違師疑 (the apparent contradiction whereby [道宣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%AE%A3) Dàoxuān, who inherited from [智首](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E9%A6%96) Zhìshǒu a "*cause-and-effect*" *zōng* 因果為宗, established a "*precept-as-zōng*" 戒為宗 of his own); and *Chāo shímén shèshǔ zhūpiān yí* 鈔十門攝屬諸篇疑 (how the ten-gate scheme of the *Shìchāo* relates to its other chapters).

The respondents are arranged in three parallel columns: each *yí* receives an answer from each of the three Sòng masters. The variation between answers is itself the source's principal scholarly value — providing a three-way controlled comparison of late-Sòng Vinaya pedagogy:
- **Liǎorán** answers from a *Tiāntái–Vinaya* integrative perspective, with frequent reference to his own *Tōngzhēn jì* ([KR6k0253](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0253)).
- **Zhìruì** answers in a more strictly *Nánshān*-traditional vein, conservative on procedural matters but doctrinally engaged.
- **Miàoyīn**, of the *Língzhī* line, gives the post-*Yuánzhào* reading.

The opening answer to *Sānguān shǐchū yí* — Liǎorán's — points the reader directly to his *Tōngzhēn jì* for the standard exposition; Zhìruì's letter-preface (15th day of the 8th month of *Jiādìng* 2 = September 15, 1209), preserved entire, frames the entire exchange as a Sino-Japanese intellectual courtesy ("*so that the schools of the two countries might together see to the bottom of the Vinaya sea*"). The colophon to *juàn xià* terminates the work without an editorial postface; it is unclear whether Shunjō or one of his Japanese disciples edited the three response-sets into the surviving combined two-fascicle form.
